Just before Apple's special event, Bloomberg published a new report detailing the decade-long development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentioned that Apple's former CEO Tim Cook had participated in this project and revealed the possible pricing of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman pointed out that Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after Cook returned from a business trip to China, he became "extremely excited" about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable device.

Cook generally "does not participate in the conception of new products," so his personal involvement in the development of the foldable iPhone gives this project more weight:

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone, internally referred to as the iPhone Ultra, Apple's original target entry-level price was US$1,999. However, due to the recent increase in component costs, the target price has been raised to US$2,199.

According to sources, Apple recently discussed pricing the foldable product as high as US$2,199, noting that different options have been considered recently, and the memory shortage has also significantly pushed up Apple's cost targets. Some models with larger storage capacities may be priced close to US$3,000. For comparison, the current starting price of the standard iPhone is US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra tomorrow for the first time. 9to5Mac will be on-site at the Steve Jobs Theater to bring you in-depth coverage of all the details.
